items.t: Gender disparities in cataract-related blindness and visual impairment: analysis of data from 204 countries
items.sum: Gender disparities exist in cataract-related vision loss, with variations across regions. Lower literacy rates, lower health expenditures, and a higher burden of cataract-blindness were associated with such disparities. Key points: Although cataract blindness declined globally by 32.2% between 1990 and 2019, gender disparities in cataract-related vision loss have persisted, and in some regions, worsened. items.t: Optimal target offset under asymmetric refractive loss and discrete intraocular lens power steps
items.src: Journal of Cataract and Refractive Surgery
items.sum: Slight myopia is often chosen during intraocular lens power selection to avoid a hyperopic result, but the appropriate offset depends on prediction uncertainty and the consequences of residual refraction.  This analysis derived the target that minimizes expected loss under unequal penalties for myopic and hyperopic outcomes and assessed discrete lens choices.

items.t: From area under the curve to clinical readiness: A framework for AI-assisted ectasia risk assessment before refractive surgery
items.sum: Artificial intelligence (AI) models for keratoconus frequently report near-perfect discrimination, with pooled sensitivity and specificity approaching 98% when manifest keratoconus is separated from normal corneas.  These figures are increasingly invoked to answer a different, more consequential question: whether an apparently non-ectatic cornea can safely undergo refractive surgery.

items.sum: The carbon footprint of most cataract surgery packs submitted to SIDICS exceeded that of the ESCRS Benchmark Pack, with drapes and gowns accounting for most pack-related emissions. items.t: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study
items.src: Journal of Cataract and Refractive Surgery
items.sum: The Moussa formula demonstrated high predictive accuracy across multiple biometry platforms, with statistically lower overall MAE than the comparator formulas. Absolute differences from the closest-performing formulas were modest, and ±0.50D outcomes were similar to Kane and EVO. These findings support Moussa as a clinically relevant contemporary option for IOL power calculation, with encouraging results in short and long eyes requiring further targeted…

items.t: Effect of implantable collamer lens on biometric measurements and intraocular lens power calculation formulas
items.sum: ICL implantation alters biometric measurements and theoretically predicted Δ-pSEQ; although these changes are statistically significant, their clinical significance is negligible. While incorrect ACD segmentation is common, it is unlikely to substantially affect the theoretical calculation
items.h_vi: Ảnh hưởng của thấu kính collamer cấy ghép đến các phép đo sinh trắc học và công thức tính công suất thấu kính nội nhãn
items.s_vi: Cấy ICL làm thay đổi các phép đo sinh trắc học và dự đoán về mặt lý thuyết Δ-pSEQ; mặc dù những thay đổi này có ý nghĩa thống kê nhưng ý nghĩa lâm sàng của chúng là không đáng kể. Mặc dù việc phân đoạn ACD không chính xác là phổ biến nhưng nó khó có thể ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến tính toán lý thuyết.
